name: Auxiliary data transfer (intermediate NLI training on MNLI/XNLI/XNLIeu, clean iSTS chunk alignments, lexical-entailment resources WordNet/MCR and PPDB 2.0, gated use of PhrasIS)

GWC 2012; EN/ES/EU/CA/GL wordnets aligned to WN3.0).
year: Resources 2012-2024 (WordNet/MCR 2012, PPDB 2013/2015, iSTS 2015/2016, MNLI/XNLI 2018, PhrasIS 2024, XNLIeu 2024); applied here for DiCo-NLI 2026-2027
license_access: All public/open: MNLI (mostly OANC, open; fiction portion with its own terms), XNLI CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, fine for research), XNLIeu same licenses as XNLI per its paper, iSTS data freely distributed for research [uncertain on exact license], PPDB CC BY 3.0, Princeton WordNet own permissive license, MCR open (CC BY 3.0 [uncertain]), PhrasIS openly available (post-print open access; data distributed with iSTS lineage) [uncertain]. External-data use is allowed by the task unless restricted in the final rules and must be declared as 'public data'.
track_coverage: T1 EN: MNLI, iSTS, PPDB 2.0, WordNet all directly usable. T2 ES: XNLI-es (MT train + human dev/test), esXNLI, MCR Spanish wordnet, Multilingual PPDB Spanish (paraphrase only, no entailment labels). T3 EU: XNLIeu (MT train + post-edited dev/test + native test), MCR Basque wordnet; no Basque PPDB [uncertain]. T4 mixed: cross-lingual NLI pairs can be built by pairing XNLI/XNLIeu premise in one language with hypothesis in another (XNLI is parallel across languages), and MCR ILI-aligned synsets give cross-lingual lexical entailment pairs (e.g. EU hyponym vs ES hypernym).
basque_quality: XNLIeu is the key Basque resource: XLM-R-large reaches 81.1 accuracy zero-shot cross-lingual and 83.8 with translate-train on XNLIeu (post-edited), 75.4 / 79.9 on the raw MT version, and 73.8 zero-shot on the native Basque test; RoBERTa-euscrawl-large (Basque monolingual) 83.0 translate-train on XNLIeu and 75.2 on native; mBERT only 60.1 zero-shot; Latxa (7B) zero-shot prompting ~51. So sentence-level Basque NLI transfer is strong for XLM-R-class encoders, and translate-train (Basque MT of MNLI) adds ~+3 points over zero-shot. MCR contains a Basque wordnet (fewer synsets than English; coverage limited to ILI-aligned nouns/verbs) that can generate hypernym/hyponym entailment pairs in Basque. No phrase-level Basque inference data exists besides the DiCo translations themselves.
cross_lingual_robustness: Intermediate NLI training on multilingual data (XNLI + XNLIeu) aligns entailment semantics across EN/ES/EU and should shrink the mixed-vs-monolingual gap in T4, since the classifier learns language-agnostic relation cues; adding explicit cross-lingual NLI pairs (premise and hypothesis in different languages, cheap to build because XNLI is parallel) targets T4 directly. Residual risk: MNLI-style sentence NLI rewards lexical overlap, which is weaker across languages, so mixed pairs may still lag monolingual ones by a few points [uncertain].
architecture: Data-side method, backbone-agnostic. Three levels of transfer: (1) Intermediate-task fine-tuning: start from an encoder already fine-tuned on MNLI(+FEVER/ANLI/LingNLI/WANLI) or on XNLI/multilingual-NLI (or run that stage yourself with XNLIeu MT train for Basque), then fine-tune on DiCo. Map 3-way NLI to DiCo either by re-initialising a 4-way head or by a bidirectional reading: entail(a->b) & entail(b->a) = EQUIVALENCE, entail(a->b) only = FORWARD_ENTAILMENT, entail(b->a) only = BACKWARD_ENTAILMENT, neither = NEGATIVE_OTHER; this reading also gives a zero-shot baseline and a strong feature. (2) Same-schema phrase data: iSTS 2015/2016 gold chunk alignments carry labels EQUI / SPE1 / SPE2 / SIMI / REL / OPPO / NOALI; SPE1 (chunk 1 more specific) maps to FORWARD_ENTAILMENT (matches DiCo convention, e.g. 'Conservative opposition' -> 'Conservatives' = FE), SPE2 to BACKWARD_ENTAILMENT, EQUI to EQUIVALENCE, SIMI/REL/OPPO/NOALI to NEGATIVE_OTHER. Only the answers-students split is disjoint from PhrasIS (PhrasIS is built from the headlines and images splits). Use as a multi-task or pre-training stage with a domain tag. (3) Lexical/phrasal entailment resources: PPDB 2.0 relation labels (Equivalence, ForwardEntailment, ReverseEntailment, Exclusion, OtherRelated, Independent) map almost 1:1 to DiCo's four labels; WordNet/MCR synonym -> EQ, hyponym->hypernym -> FE, hypernym->hyponym -> BE, co-hyponyms/antonyms -> NEG; optionally embed them into templated phrases ('a [hyponym] on the street' vs 'a [hypernym] on the street') to mimic chunk structure. Every auxiliary pair should be added in both directions with the reversed label so the auxiliary signal is itself reversal-consistent.
params: No extra parameters; uses the backbone (184M-560M encoders). Data sizes: MNLI 393k train; XNLI 392k MT train per language + 2,490 dev / 5,010 test human-translated per language; XNLIeu ~393k MT train + post-edited dev/test of XNLI size [uncertain]; PPDB 2.0 English tens of millions of pairs (S size ~ a few million lexical/phrasal pairs with relation labels) [uncertain]; iSTS answers-students roughly 1-2k aligned chunk pairs per year [uncertain]; PhrasIS 10,214 phrase pairs (4,918 headlines, 5,296 images) of which ~1,946 reversible (the DiCo source set).
compute: Using a published NLI checkpoint costs nothing extra. Running your own intermediate stage: one epoch of MNLI (393k short pairs) on DeBERTa-v3-large or XLM-R-large takes roughly 2-4 GPU-hours on a single 24 GB GPU with bf16 and max_len 128; XNLI+XNLIeu multilingual stage 3-10 GPU-hours depending on language subset [uncertain]. Phrase-level resources (iSTS, WordNet/PPDB samples of 10-50k pairs) add minutes. Fits a 24 GB card; no multi-GPU needed.
sample_efficiency: This is the main lever for the small-data regime (T1 train: 1,282 reversible source pairs + 478 NEG singletons; dev: 277 + 106). Intermediate NLI training is well documented to help small target sets and to reduce seed variance/fine-tuning collapse (Pruksachatkun et al. 2020 find MNLI among the most reliably helpful intermediate tasks, especially for small targets). Expected to reduce run-to-run variance on DiCo, but the domain mismatch (sentence NLI vs phrase-level specificity) means gains saturate quickly; lexical-entailment data targets exactly the hypernymy/specificity errors reported in the pilot error analysis.
reported_results: Pilot DiCo (English, no intermediate NLI training reported): DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75 W-F1 / 0.84 SoftCons / 0.79 HardCons; encoder family mean 0.713 / 0.770 / 0.721. XNLIeu: XLM-R-large 81.1 zero-shot / 83.8 translate-train; native Basque test 73.8 zero-shot; RoBERTa-euscrawl-large 83.0 translate-train (XNLIeu) and 75.2 (native). A 2025 follow-up on Basque/Spanish dialectal NLI (CoNLL 2025, 'Lost in Variation?') reports XLM-RoBERTa translate-train 83.42 on XNLIeu and 73.21 on dialectal XNLIeu-var. MoritzLaurer DeBERTa-v3-large-mnli-fever-anli-ling-wanli reports ~91-92 MNLI-m accuracy; mDeBERTa-v3-base-xnli-multilingual-nli-2mil7 ~87 average XNLI [uncertain]. PhrasIS original paper: inter-annotator agreement accuracy 0.78 (headlines, kappa 0.66) and 0.82 (images, kappa 0.77) over the full label set, which bounds achievable phrase-level accuracy; its classic baselines (SVM, RF, LSTM) reached ~0.4-0.5 F1 on positive labels only. No published phrase-level results for iSTS/PPDB/WordNet transfer to DiCo.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot (Apaolaza Larraya et al.), which fine-tuned vanilla pretrained checkpoints (ModernBERT, ALBERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTa-v3, OPT, Pythia, GPT-2, BART, Flan-T5) directly on PhrasIS-derived data with Optuna hyperparameter search; NLI intermediate training is not mentioned, so the pilot numbers (best 0.75 / 0.84 / 0.79) are a no-transfer baseline.
consistency_guarantee: none (soft at best: adding every auxiliary pair in both directions with reversed labels teaches reversal-equivariance as a data prior, but gives no guarantee; combine with joint decoding or an antisymmetric head)
negative_other_handling: Auxiliary data enriches the NEG class: iSTS SIMI/REL/OPPO/NOALI, PPDB Exclusion/OtherRelated/Independent, WordNet co-hyponyms/antonyms, and MNLI neutral/contradiction (under the bidirectional reading). Caveat: DiCo NEG is a mapped mixture of PhrasIS SIMI/REL/OPPO/unrelated pairs with high lexical overlap (e.g. 'at an airfield' / 'in an airport', 'Two ducks' / 'The birds' are NEG), so aux NEG definitions differ (PPDB/WordNet would call 'Two ducks' -> 'The birds' forward entailment). Down-weight or drop aux NEG and hypernym examples whose semantics conflict with PhrasIS conventions; tune the NEG threshold on DiCo OOF predictions after transfer. Yes, the resulting model can emit NEG on reversible pairs; aux data does not change that.
metric_tradeoff: Primarily improves Weighted F1 and HardCons via better per-direction accuracy on EQ/FE/BE (specificity and hypernymy knowledge); SoftCons gains are indirect (a more accurate model is more consistent) unless auxiliary pairs are added in both directions. Risk: label-convention mismatch on NEG vs FE (PhrasIS annotators label many taxonomic pairs as SIMI/REL) can lower NEG precision and W-F1 if aux data is weighted too heavily.
integration: (a) Zero-cost: set model_name to an NLI checkpoint and load with AutoModelForSequenceClassification(num_labels=4, ignore_mismatched_sizes=True), or keep the 3-way head and derive 4-way probabilities with the bidirectional reading as an extra feature/ensemble member. (b) Two-stage training script: stage 1 on aux mixture (XNLI+XNLIeu, iSTS answers-students, PPDB/MCR samples mapped to DiCo labels via src/labels.py LABELS, every pair duplicated reversed with REVERSE_PERM), stage 2 on DiCo train. (c) Multi-task: single 4-way head, mixed batches with a per-source loss weight (e.g. 0.1-0.3 for aux). Data loaders should output the DiCo CSV schema (instance_id, pair_id, text1_lang, text2_lang, text1, text2, label) with an 'aux_' pair_id prefix so grouped CV never mixes aux and target groups.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes: produces standard 4-way softmax outputs; transfer-initialised models are usually better calibrated at start but still need temperature scaling on OOF/dev before pooling with joint decoding.
inference_cost: Unchanged from the backbone: one forward pass per test row (~4k rows per monolingual track, ~24k in T4), seconds to minutes on one GPU.
rules_disclosure: Declare External data use = 'public data' and list every resource (MNLI, XNLI, XNLIeu, iSTS 2015/2016 splits used, PPDB 2.0, WordNet/MCR, and PhrasIS if used) plus any published checkpoints already trained on them; architecture family and access regime follow the backbone (encoder-only, open-weight). The FAQ states the final policy will require reporting any use of PhrasIS or related public datasets and may restrict it; the final rules must be checked before submission.
contamination: High-risk area. DiCo is derived from PhrasIS, which is derived from iSTS 2015/2016 headlines and images chunk alignments; PhrasIS has ~1,946 reversible EN source pairs in total and DiCo train+dev already contain 1,559 of them (1,282 + 277, verified on the released files), so the remaining ~387 reversible PhrasIS pairs are almost certainly the English test pairs and their gold labels are public in PhrasIS and (as SPE1/SPE2/EQUI) in the iSTS gold alignment files. Training on raw PhrasIS or iSTS headlines/images is therefore test leakage for T1 and, via translation, for T2-T4, and would likely violate the rule that hidden evaluation labels must not be used. Safe practice: (1) use only iSTS answers-students (not in PhrasIS) plus generic NLI/lexical resources; (2) if the organizers permit PhrasIS, use only its non-reversible pairs and remove every pair whose phrases (case/whitespace-normalised) match any test input once test inputs are released, and document the filter; (3) MNLI/XNLI/PPDB/WordNet have no meaningful overlap with PhrasIS phrases beyond generic short noun phrases. Pretrained backbones may have seen PhrasIS/iSTS text (not labels) in web crawls; low risk. Pending PhrasIS policy.
structural_cue_dependence: None. Auxiliary transfer only changes the learned classifier; it does not use pair_id, twin presence, or singleton heuristics.
priority: P0 for starting from an NLI-fine-tuned checkpoint (MNLI/XNLI/multilingual-NLI; plus XNLIeu for Basque) since it is free and low-risk; P1 for iSTS answers-students + PPDB/MCR lexical-entailment augmentation; P2 / blocked for any PhrasIS use until the official data-use policy is published (and never the reversible PhrasIS subset).
expected_gain: NLI intermediate checkpoint vs vanilla backbone: +2 to +5 W-F1 and a similar HardCons gain on T1, larger on T3 EU where the backbone has least supervision (XNLIeu translate-train showed ~+3 over zero-shot at sentence level) [uncertain]; lower seed variance. Lexical-entailment and iSTS answers-students augmentation: +0.5 to +2 W-F1, concentrated on FE/BE specificity errors (the pilot error analysis highlights taxonomic relations, near-synonymy and world knowledge), with a risk of hurting NEG precision if convention mismatch is not controlled [uncertain]. Using raw PhrasIS would inflate scores dramatically but is leakage and must not be counted as a gain.
